target-environments.value: Local Windows, macOS, and Linux with Node.js 24 or newer; supported MCP stdio clients; and production-like npm package staging.

browsers-devices.value: Agent Bridge itself has no browser requirement. Its public documentation must pass Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit plus responsive viewport coverage from 320px through 4K.

test-data.value: Use examples/basic, the canonical Agent Bridge CocoSpec and CocoQA records, and isolated temporary directories. Do not use credentials, secrets, external services, production accounts, or production data; remove temporary fixtures after each test.

release-blockers.value: Every required gate, critical or high defect, workspace escape, sensitive-output exposure, protocol incompatibility, and read-only guarantee violation blocks release. Only low-risk non-security findings may be waived with explicit framework maintainer approval.

accessibility-target.value: Public documentation must meet WCAG 2.2 AA, including semantic headings, descriptive links, keyboard-only navigation, visible focus, logical focus order, screen-reader labels, zoom support, and responsive readability. The stdio Agent Bridge itself has no visual interface.

security-abuse.value: Negative tests must cover malformed input, unsupported protocol versions, path traversal, symlink or junction workspace escape, invalid workspaces, cancellation, response and file limits, secret and authorization-header redaction, stdout protocol cleanliness, mutation refusal, absence of arbitrary shell execution, and prevention of AI self-approval or permission widening.

cases.title: Given a supported AI client, when it connects through MCP, then it can discover every Agent Bridge tool together with its versioned input schema, output schema, description, and permission level.
cases.evidence: tests/agent.test.ts completes MCP initialize and tools/list, asserting five tools with descriptions, versioned input/output schemas, and read permission metadata.

cases.title: Given a valid CocoFrame workspace, when project.inspect is called, then it returns the existing routes, APIs, components, islands, middleware, dependencies, and generated capabilities without modifying the workspace.
cases.evidence: project.inspect returns routes, APIs, components, islands, middleware, dependencies, and generated capabilities; before/after file metadata remains identical.

cases.title: Given an existing framework capability, when the AI searches documentation, APIs, or components, then Agent Bridge returns the reusable capability and its source or documentation location before suggesting a new implementation.
cases.evidence: Focused tests verify docs.search, component.find, and api.lookup return reusable capabilities with source or documentation locations.

cases.title: Given a new feature request, when the AI starts or resumes CocoSpecs, then Agent Bridge returns only the next adaptive question batch and preserves the canonical specification state.
cases.evidence: Agent lifecycle tests verify proposed and canonical CocoSpecs return only the bounded next adaptive batch and preserve before/after workspace state.

cases.title: Given an image or website reference, when CocoRef is invoked, then existing components are audited before a missing component is proposed.
cases.evidence: Agent lifecycle tests verify CocoRef audits the inspected component inventory, reuses Button, and marks only the unmatched timeline as consent-required.

cases.title: Given an implemented feature with an approved CocoSpec, when CocoQA is invoked, then acceptance criteria, required gates, evidence, defects, and approval state remain traceable.
cases.evidence: Agent lifecycle tests verify approved-CocoSpec QA traceability includes acceptance criteria, questions, cases, gates, sanitized evidence, defects, and approval state.

cases.title: Given a read-only operation, when it is executed, then no source file, generated artifact, Git state, package state, or external system is changed.
cases.evidence: Read-only tests compare the complete example workspace file state before and after MCP discovery and find no changes.

cases.title: Given an operation that may change state, when explicit approval has not been granted, then Agent Bridge refuses the operation and leaves all state unchanged.
cases.evidence: Unknown mutation tool file.write is refused with CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE and the workspace remains unchanged; Phase 1 exposes no state-changing tool.

cases.title: Given an approved mutation, when the operation is executed, then only the declared workspace targets and declared action are modified.
cases.evidence: Phase 3 mutation tests verify exact current/proposed hashes, role-bound partial approval, unchanged undeclared targets, single-use execution, target conflict detection, and multi-file rollback.

cases.title: Given a denied, expired, or cancelled approval, when execution is attempted, then no mutation occurs and a stable machine-readable diagnostic is returned.
cases.evidence: Phase 3 mutation tests verify denied, cancelled, expired, duplicate, and already-claimed approvals return stable diagnostics and leave every declared source target unchanged.

cases.title: Given any workspace path supplied by an AI client, when it resolves outside the approved project root, then Agent Bridge rejects access.
cases.evidence: A junction resolving outside the approved root is rejected with WORKSPACE_ACCESS_DENIED without exposing or reading the outside file.

cases.title: Given malformed input or an unsupported protocol version, when a tool is called, then Agent Bridge returns a versioned corrective error without crashing.
cases.evidence: MCP malformed input returns structured INVALID_TOOL_INPUT; unsupported bridge versions and cancellation return versioned corrective diagnostics without crashing.

cases.title: Given secrets, cookies, authorization headers, tokens, or request bodies exist in the environment, when results and errors are returned, then none of those sensitive values are exposed or persisted.
cases.evidence: Documentation containing an Authorization bearer secret is searched with the secret removed and REDACTED evidence returned; raw secret is never persisted.

cases.title: Given two supported AI providers, when they perform the same Agent Bridge workflow, then they use the same provider-independent tool contracts and receive structurally equivalent results.
cases.evidence: The bridge uses the official provider-neutral MCP server contract with no provider branches; raw MCP client discovery receives the same structural tool results.

cases.title: Given a completed workflow, when the AI reports completion, then the result includes the actions performed, approvals received, files or artifacts affected, quality evidence, and unresolved risks.
cases.evidence: Canonical CocoQA artifacts and the implementation handoff report actions, approvals, affected files, automated evidence, blocked full-scope cases, and unresolved risks.

cases.title: Useful server-rendered output exists without browser JavaScript.
cases.evidence: Agent Bridge has no browser runtime and its public guide renders server-side; production browser runtime tests pass.

cases.title: Keyboard, focus, labels, errors, and semantic structure satisfy the approved accessibility target.
cases.evidence: Agent Bridge documentation uses semantic headings and links; keyboard and accessibility browser assertions pass across the official matrix.

cases.title: The feature remains usable across the approved viewport and device range without horizontal overflow.
cases.evidence: The critical-page matrix includes /docs/agent-bridge and the filtered Agent API reference and passes at 320px, phone, tablet, laptop, and 4K viewports.
